Which undergraduate (UG) programs are available at RBPU? UG programs include B.Tech (multiple specializations), BCA (AI, Data Science, Cloud, Cyber Security, IoT), BBA, B.Com (Hons), BA, B.Sc, B.Pharm, D.Pharm, LLB, BA LLB, BBA LLB, B.Sc Nursing, GNM, BHMCT, BJMC, etc. What postgraduate (PG) courses does Rayat Bahra Professional University offer? The university would implement various measures to ensure that students with disabilities can fully participate in campus life without facing physical, social, or academic barriers. These facilities would be designed to promote independence, inclusion, and accessibility, allowing differently-abled students to thrive both academically and personally. Physical Infrastructure and Accessibility The university would ensure that its campus infrastructure is fully accessible to students with physical disabilities. This would include the installation of ramps, elevators, and wide doorways in key areas such as classrooms, libraries, laboratories, hostels, and common areas. Accessible washrooms and toilets would be available in all major buildings. Additionally, pathways and entrances would be clearly marked with signage and directional aids for ease of navigation. The campus would be designed to ensure that students with mobility impairments can move around freely without encountering physical obstacles. Assistive Technologies and Learning Resources Rayat Bahra Professional University would equip its classrooms and computer labs with assistive technologies such as screen readers, audio books, speech-to-text software, and magnification tools. These technologies would assist students with visual impairments, hearing disabilities, and learning challenges, enabling them to access learning materials in alternative formats. Furthermore, e-learning platforms and online resources would be made available to accommodate various learning needs, allowing students to learn at their own pace and convenience. Faculty members would be trained to use these tools effectively and offer additional support to differently-abled students. Specialized Support Services The university would offer personalized academic support for students with disabilities, including note-taking assistance, extended exam time, and special seating arrangements. Dedicated academic counselors would be available to help these students with course material, study techniques, and exam preparation. The Equal Opportunity Cell (EOC) would work closely with the Disability Support Services to ensure that students with special needs are aware of the resources available to them and can access the necessary accommodations. Hostel and Residential Facilities Accessible accommodation would be available in the university’s hostels, with features such as wheelchair-accessible rooms, adjustable beds, and specialized equipment to support students with mobility challenges. The hostel facilities would ensure that differently-abled students feel comfortable and independent in their living spaces. The university would also ensure that common areas like kitchens, dining halls, and recreational spaces are accessible and inclusive, providing the necessary infrastructure for students to participate in daily activities. Transportation and Mobility Assistance Rayat Bahra Professional University would provide accessible transportation services for differently-abled students, including specialized shuttle buses or vans equipped with ramps or lifts to ensure safe and easy travel across campus. Additionally, wheelchair assistance would be available for students who require support during their movement between different buildings and facilities. The campus would have designated parking spaces close to key entrances to accommodate students and staff with disabilities. Counseling and Mental Health Support Psychological and emotional support would be available for differently-abled students through the university’s counseling services. These services would focus on not only helping students cope with academic challenges but also addressing any social or psychological issues they may face as a result of their disability. The counselors would work with students to promote mental well-being, reduce any feelings of isolation, and offer support in overcoming personal barriers. Awareness and Sensitization Programs To promote a more inclusive and empathetic campus culture, Rayat Bahra Professional University would regularly organize awareness programs and sensitization workshops aimed at both students and faculty. These programs would focus on fostering a deeper understanding of the challenges faced by differently-abled students and how the university community can better support them. Such initiatives would help reduce stigma and promote equality for students

chunks.text: Equal Opportunity Cell | Rayat Bahra Professional University (RBPU) Main Links About Academics Programs Campus Life Admissions Placements Research Career Centre Contact Us University Links Ph.D. Registration Equal Opportunities Cell (EOC) In pursuance of the provisions contained in the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2012, and in compliance with UGC D.O. No. 1-2/2024 (SCT/Circular) dated 10th January 2025, regarding establishment of Equal Opportunity and SC/ST Cells in Higher Educational Institutions, we are pleased to constitute the Equal Opportunities Cell (EOC) at Rayat Bahra Professional University, Hoshiarpur. The Equal Opportunities Cell shall function as a statutory facilitation and grievance redressal mechanism to ensure equity, inclusion, and non-discrimination in all academic and administrative processes of the University. Composition of the Committee Sr.no. Member Details Designation 1 Dr. Jarnail Singh, Director & HOD, University School of Computer Application Chairman 2 Mr. Mohit Chander, Faculty Representative Member 3 Student Representative (1st year students preferably from disadvantaged group) to be nominated by the Chairman Member 4 Ms. Rashmi Sharma Educationist / Advocate / NGO Representative 5 Dr. Priyanka Puri, Nodal Officer Member Secretary Functions A. Grievance Redressal Address complaints relating to discrimination, harassment and denial of equal opportunity. Recommend corrective and disciplinary measures to competent authorities. Ensure confidentiality and time-bound resolution. B. Student Support & Inclusion Provide academic support, mentoring, and counselling to disadvantaged students. Facilitate access to scholarships, fellowships, and welfare schemes. Promote inclusive teaching-learning practices. C. Policy Implementation & Monitoring Ensure effective implementation of policies in admissions, scholarships, and recruitment as per norms. Monitor compliance with UGC directions issued from time to time. Maintain database of students and staff belonging to disadvantaged groups. D. Compliance of PwD Act, 2016 Ensure barrier-free access to infrastructure (ramps, lifts, accessible toilets, signage). Provide assistive technologies, scribes, and examination accommodations. Implement various provisions under the Act. E. Coordination Coordinate with different committees like SC/ST Cell, PwD Cell, Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), Anti-Ragging Committee etc. Submit periodic compliance reports to university authorities and UGC (as required). F. Awareness & Capacity Building Organize sensitization programmes, workshops, and outreach activities. Promote awareness about constitutional values, equality, and diversity. Scope and Applicability The provisions of the Equal Opportunities Cell shall apply to all students, faculty members, and staff of the University. Tenure / Duration The Equal Opportunities Cell / Committee shall remain in force for a period of three (03) years from the date of issuance of this notification or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Sd/- Vice Chancellor Rayat and Bahra Professional University Hoshiarpur

chunks.text: Grievance Redressal Committee | Rayat Bahra Professional University (RBPU) Main Links About Academics Programs Campus Life Admissions Placements Research Career Centre Contact Us University Links Ph.D. Registration STUDENT GRIEVANCES REDRESSAL COMMITTEE As per the UGC Regulations on Redressal of Grievance of Students - 2023, issued vide the Gazette of India CG-DL-E-11042023-245095 EXTRAORDINARY PART III-section 4 on 11/04/2023, RBPU has set up the below mentioned Grievances Redressal Committee from the Academic Year 2025-26 onwards to redress the Complaints/Grievances of the students. 1. Constitution of Student Grievances Redressal Committee Stage Description Stage 1 Constitution of Grievances Redressal Committee at the level of School/Department (DGRC) Stage 2 Constitution of University Student Grievances Redressal Committee (SGRC) Stage 3 Appointment of Ombudsperson 2. Composition of Department/School Grievances Redressal Committee (DGRC) The Department/School level Grievances Committee (DGRC) shall address all issues of the student related to the concerned school/department. The student shall submit his/her complaint to the member secretary of the DGRC. S.No. Designation Position 1 Dean / Associate Dean / HOD Chairperson 2 Two faculties from the department at the Senior level Member 3 One representative of students nominated by the respective Dean/HOD of the School/Department. Member 4 Programme Coordinator Member Secretary 3. Composition of Student Grievances Redressal Committee at University Level (SGRC) The University level Student Grievances Redressal Committee (SGRC) shall consider all such complaints which are not resolved at the DGRC level of the School/Department. S.No. Name Designation Position 1 Dr. Kuldeep Walia Dean, Student Welfare Chairperson 2 Dr. Jyotsana Dean, School of Basic Sciences Member 3 Dr. Jasdeep Kaur Dhami Dean, IQAC Member 4 Mr. Kuldeep Rana Director, Administration Member 5 Ms. Rashmi Sharma Educationist/Advocate/NGO representative Member 6 Student Representative To be nominated by the Dean of the concerned School Member 7 Dr. Maninderpal Singh Associate Dean, School of Pharmaceutical Sciences Member Secretary The term of the members including Chairperson shall be two years. The term of the student representative shall be one year. The quorum for the meeting excluding the student representative shall be three. 4. Procedure for Submission of Complaints by Student to SGRC Aggrieved student shall write to the member secretary of the Grievance Redressal Committee at the department/school level (DGRC). If student believes that, his/her problem is not resolved he/she can appeal to the University Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) addressed to the member secretary of SGRC with supporting documents seeking redressal of grievance. The member secretary shall coordinate with the student for further action. 5. The Procedure Adopted by the Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) and Ombudsperson On receipt of a complaint by the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC), along with comments of the committee (DGRC) within 15 days of receipt of the complaint. The Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) of the University shall fix a date for hearing the complaint, which shall be communicated to the Dean/HOD of the respective department/school and to the aggrieved student. Student Grievance Redressal Committee shall ensure disposal of every application as early as possible, not later than three weeks, from receipt of the grievance. On the conclusion of proceedings, the Student Grievance Redressal Committee shall pass such order, as may be deemed fit to redress the grievance and provide such relief as may be desirable to the affected student. The SGRC shall send its report with recommendations, to the Vice Chancellor of the University and a copy thereof to the aggrieved student preferably within 15 working days from the date of receipt of the complaint, however not later than 21 days. Grievances not resolved by the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee within the time given then shall be referred to the Ombudsperson within 15 days from the decision of final decision delivered by SGRC. The Ombudsperson shall, after giving reasonable opportunities of being heard to the parties concerned, on the conclusion of proceedings, pass such order, with reasons thereof, as may be deemed fit to redress the grievance. chunks.text: Nodal Officer for Student Well-Being | Rayat Bahra Professional University (RBPU) Main Links About Academics Programs Campus Life Admissions Placements Research Career Centre Contact Us University Links Ph.D. Registration Appointment of Nodal Officer for Student Well-Being, Crisis Response and Compliance Office Memorandum dated 05.02.2026 issued by the Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education, forwarding the Hon’ble Supreme Court Orders dated 15.01.2026 in Amit Kumar & Others vs. Union of India & Others, requested necessary action based on the directions contained therein, along with monthly status / action reporting. Accordingly, one of the directions issued is for strict compliance of nomination of a Nodal Officer for Student Well-Being, Crisis Response and Compliance. Nomination of Nodal Officer for Student Well-Being, Crisis Response and Compliance Every University and every Centre of Legal Education shall designate a senior responsible officer not below the rank of Registrar, Principal, Director, Dean or equivalent as the Nodal Officer for Student Well-Being, Crisis Response, and Compliance. Roles and Responsibilities The Nodal Officer shall be responsible for: Immediate crisis response. Referral and medical coordination. Compliance and police intimation obligations. Preservation of records. Communication with authorities. Institutional follow-up. Preparation and transmission of compliance records. Display of Nodal Officer Details The name, designation, mobile number and email address of the Nodal Officer shall be displayed on the University website and student notice boards. Mandatory Institutional Mechanisms Every University and every Centre of Legal Education shall ensure the active constitution, formal notification and effective functioning of the following: Anti-Ragging Committee Anti-Ragging Squad Student Grievance Redressal Committee Internal Complaints Committee or other legally compliant complaint-handling mechanism for sexual harassment and gender-based grievances Anti-Discrimination / Equal Opportunity mechanism, wherever applicable Counselling and Wellness Centre or documented referral arrangement Internal oversight mechanism for mental health and student support review The constitution of other committees as above shall be taken up separately. 30.03.2026 Vice Chancellor Rajesh Moza Registrar

It ensures that projects stick to the ethical principles—such as autonomy, beneficence, and justice—as well as legal, regulatory, and scientific standards. The committee will have a tenure of 3 years from the date of issue of this notification. Following is the constitution of the committee: - Constitution of the Committee Sr. No. Name Designation Position 1 Prof. Chander Mohan Vice Chancellor Chairman 2 Prof. Gaurav Bhardwaj Professor & Dean, Punjab Technical University Member 3 Prof. Jasdeep Kaur Dhami Professor & Dean, RBPU Member 4 Dr. Nikhil Monga Associate Dean, USBS, RBPU Member 5 Dr. Maninderpal Singh Associate Dean, USPS, RBPU Member 6 Dr. Gaurav Parashar Associate Professor, USE, RBPU Member Terms of Reference of the Committee Protocol Review: To evaluate research proposals to ensure ethical standards are met before studies begin. Informed Consent: To ensure participants are well informed and voluntarily agree to participate. Risk-Benefit Analysis: To assess, whether expected benefits from research justify risks or hardships to the participants. Monitoring: To monitor approved research projects for ongoing ethical compliance. Education: To train researchers, staff, and students on ethical guidelines. Autonomy: To respect the rights and dignity of individuals. Justice: To ensure fair distribution of research risks and benefits.

chunks.text: SC/ST Cell | Rayat Bahra Professional University (RBPU) Main Links About Academics Programs Campus Life Admissions Placements Research Career Centre Contact Us University Links Ph.D. Registration SC/ST Cell The SC/ST Cell is a statutory body prescribed by UGC to ensure the effective implementation of government policies regarding SC/ST, provide a supportive environment, and address the grievances of students and staff belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). This cell acts as a bridge between the university administration and SC/ST individuals, upholding the constitutional mandate for social justice and equity. The committee has a tenure of 3 years from the issue of this notification. Following is the composition of the Cell: 1. Composition of the Cell Sr. No. Member Details Designation 1 Dr. Jarnail Singh, Director & HOD, USCA Chairman 2 Dr. Priyanka Puri, HOD, School of Law Liaison Officer 3 Mr. Mohit Chander, Assistant Professor, RBPU Member Secretary 4 Mr. Parminder Singh, Superintendent (Staff Representative) Member 2. Terms of Reference of the Committee The SC/ST cell serves multiple functions aimed at empowerment and grievance redressal: Implementation of Government Policies : Monitoring and enforcing the government policies for SC/ST candidates. Grievance Redressal : Functioning as a specialized cell to resolve academic, administrative, and social grievances of SC/ST students and employees. Awareness and Information Dissemination : Circulating information regarding Government of India, State Government, and UGC directives concerning scholarships, fellowships, and other welfare schemes. Data Collection and Reporting : Maintaining updated data on the enrolment, dropout rates, and employment of SC/ST individuals, and submitting required annual reports to the UGC. Support and Mentoring : Providing guidance and counselling to SC/ST students on academic and personal matters to help them manage university life effectively. Remedial Coaching : Organizing remedial coaching and skill-upgradation programs to bring SC/ST students at par with the general student body. Safe and Secure Environment : Ensuring a campus environment free from discrimination, caste-based harassment, or exploitation. Coordinate with other committees : SC/ST Cell shall coordinate with other committees on different issues, if required, particularly with the Equal Opportunities Cell. Sd/- Vice Chancellor

chunks.text: Examination Process Main Links About Academics Programs Campus Life Admissions Placements Research Career Centre Contact Us University Links Ph.D. Registration Examination Process At the core of the growing popularity of Rayat-Bahra Professional University among students and parents is the industry-focused curriculum that enables students to become employment- ready by the time they complete their course. The University believes in making learning effective by involving and engaging the students in various interdisciplinary and co-curricular activities. To help students adapt easily to the industry environment, the University has made Domain Skills, Soft Skills, and Industry Interface an integral part of its Curricula. In addition, the University aims to develop world-class Entrepreneurs with its focus on Entrepreneurship Skill Development with International Exposure. Important Aspects of the Examination Process 1. Registration Candidates shall have to register as bonafide students with the University as per regulations before the commencement of instruction in the first semester and for lateral entry students in the 3rd semester. A student is allowed to attend classes only for those subjects that the student has registered in a semester. 2. Mandatory Requirement of Attendance A student must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each of the campus-based courses without which the student shall be disqualified from appearing in the respective examinations and the student is required to register again (RRA) in the course. 3. Conduct of Mid-Term Test Two MST’s will be conducted in one semester as per the academic calendar by the concerned Schools. The MST shall be conducted as per the norms of the University. 4. Continuous Evaluation The continuous evaluation will include the MST results, and other components such as tutorials, laboratory exercises/viva/project files, home assignments, several quizzes/class tests, the regularity of attendance, etc. 5. Conduct of End Term Exam On the basis of the Academic Calendar, the date sheet for the End Semester examination shall be conveyed to the concerned Schools at least two weeks prior to the start of end term exams. The COE will get the answer books evaluated by table marking by the set of examiners. 6. Compilation and Declaration of Result At the conclusion of the semester, a student is awarded a grade in each of the courses the student has taken during that period. The grade awarded to a student in a course will depend on total performance in all components of the evaluation. Every student must appear in MST-1, MST-2, and End Term Examination. For D. Pharmacy and B. Pharmacy Practice courses, three MST’s during the session are mandatory. 7. Minimum Academic Requirements At the end of every semester, the following minimum academic standards have to be maintained by students: A student should have an SGPA of at least 4.0 for diploma & undergraduate courses and SGPA 4.5 for postgraduate courses. A minimum CGPA of 4.00 for diploma & UG, and CGPA 4.0 for PG courses is achieved. The student has not exceeded the maximum time specified for course completion. Students who fulfill the graduation criteria will be issued a provisional degree/certificate. 9. Classification of Graduation Certificates Classification Criteria Distinction CGPA ≥ 8.00 First Division CGPA ≥ 6.00 but < 8.00 Second Division (Diploma/UG) CGPA ≥ 5.00 but < 6.00 Second Division (PG) CGPA ≥ 5.50 but < 6.00 10. Organizing idea competitions, hackathons, bootcamps, and entrepreneurship development programs.
